title: Quantization-Triggered Backdoors Bypass Full-Precision Model Safety Checks
plain: Researchers built a three-stage adversarial fine-tuning framework that embeds latent malicious payloads into models which pass standard source-precision safety checks, but activate targeted misbehavior once compressed with INT8 or 4-bit post-training quantization. angles.claim: Any safety sign-off that names a model version without naming its quantization configuration is not a valid sign-off and should be rejected on Thursday.
angles.audience: Director asking what to demand from vendors and internal teams before accepting a certification
angles.rank_reason: Directly changes what gets asked in governance review and closes a control gap that many regulated deployments currently treat as satisfied

angles.claim: Engineers should add a quantized-artifact regression suite to CI before edge deployment, since the FP16 checkpoint and the shipped INT8 or 4-bit model are functionally different products.
angles.audience: Engineer deciding what changes in the deployment pipeline on Monday
angles.rank_reason: Reaches the same production systems as the top angle but is a build step rather than an accountability rule, so it changes fewer decisions outside engineering

angles.claim: Buying a third-party fine-tuned checkpoint transfers a hidden liability, because the seller's safety claim covers a precision you will not actually run in production.
angles.audience: Director or procurement lead evaluating external model suppliers
angles.rank_reason: Extends the article's finding into a supply-chain contract question it does not raise, but is more speculative and harder to act on immediately than the certification and CI angles
